Dated this the 5th day of February, 2025 The 3rd respondent in O.P.(M.V.) No.1426/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pathanamthitta is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the wife, parents and sister of the deceased by name Albert Chandran, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.4.2012.

According to them, on 29.4.2012, while the deceased was travelling in a motorcycle, he was hit down by a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KL 15-6585, driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which he sustained very serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries, on the same day.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner, and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due 2025:KER:10010 to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.68,59,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A14.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.58,35,000/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the Respondent No. 3 preferred this appeal.
8. Now, the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

sentences.text: 2 9. Heard Sri.Mathew Jacob, the learned Senior Standing Counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent/appellant and Sri. A. N Santhosh, the learned Counsel for the petitioners.
The Point:

One of the arguments raised by the learned Senior Counsel for the 3rd respondent is that in the final report filed by the police in the crime in respect to the above accident, the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the KSRTC bus were made accused 1 and 2 respectively.

Therefore, according to him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the KSRTC bus and as such, the Tribunal was not justified in mulcting the entire liability on the 3 rd respondent.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon the evidence of PW1 to submit that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the 1st respondent and hence it was argued that the Tribunal was justified in finding that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the 1st respondent.

11. It is true that in Ext.A7 charge sheet in Crime No.612 of 2012 of Pandalam Police Station, the rider of the motorcycle was made the 1st accused, and the driver of the KSRTC bus, the 1st respondent herein, is made as the 2nd accused.

However, when PW1, one of the charge witnesses cited by the prosecution was examined before the court, he deposed that the motorcycle came from the lane on the western side and crossed the MC road 2025:KER:10010 and reached the eastern side, and only at that time, the KSRTC bus, which came from the southern side, hit against the motorcycle.
According to him, the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the 1 st respondent.
In this case, the Tribunal has relied upon the evidence of PW1 to come to the conclusion that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the 1st respondent.

12. The law is well settled that the charge sheet filed by the police after investigating the crime in respect to the accident is prima facie evidence of negligence against the accused in the charge sheet.
However, the finding of the police in the charge sheet is not binding when there is any evidence to the contrary.
In this case, as noted by the Tribunal, PW1 has categorically deposed about the incident and deposed that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 1st respondent.
In this context, it is also to be noted that the respondents did not adduce any evidence to controvert the evidence of PW1.
The driver of the KSRTC bus, namely the 1 st respondent, is the fit person who could speak about the reason for the accident.
However, he has not entered the witness box to swear about the manner in which the accident occurred, without offering an explanation.
In the above circumstances, in the light of 2025:KER:10010 the available evidence, the Tribunal was justified in finding that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the 1st respondent.
13. Another contentions raised by the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent is that the notional income of the deceased fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.27,000/- is on the higher side.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was working as Electrical Supervisor in Gulf, earning a monthly income of Rs.45,000/-.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner relied upon Exhibit A7 bank statement and Exhibit A10 passport.
From Exhibit A10 passport, it is revealed that the deceased returned from Gulf on 26.3.2012, within a period of one month before the accident.

From Exhibit A8 bank statement, it is revealed that during the year 2009, there was regular remittance in the said account The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Jibi E.S on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107303577/
3 and average remittance will come to Rs.20,000/-.

sentences.text: However, during the year 2012, no such remittance is seen.

14. Learned counsel for the petitioners produced a printout, which he claims to be downloaded from the website of Labour Department of Kerala Government, showing that the daily minimum wage rate of an Electrical Wire-man during the year 2012-2013, was Rs.638/-.
The authenticity of which is not challenged by the 3rd respondent.
Therefore, the monthly income 2025:KER:10010 of a daily wage Electrical Worker will come to Rs.16,588/- (638x26).

Since in this case it is revealed that the deceased was an Electrical Supervisor working abroad, his notional income is fixed at Rs.18,000/-
15.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 30 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: Since the deceased had 3 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.34,27,200/-.
16.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.1,00,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and each dependent is entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three 2025:KER:10010 years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.
Towards loss of consortium, petitioners are entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,45,200/- (48,400 x 3).

17. Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, (2020)9 SCC 644.

18. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation.
Considering the facts, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for compensation towards pain and suffering.
Hence Rs.25,000/- is awarded on that head.
19. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

20. Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.36,35,700 /-,

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.36,35,700/- (Rupees Thirty Six Lakh Thirty Five Thousand Seven Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation/deposit, within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
